text:
Alex Tuch's biggest week had nothing to do with hockey. In a Players' Tribune essay, the Syracuse-area native thanked the nurses at Sisters Hospital in Buffalo for saving his newborn son's life. It is a reminder that the season on the ice is only part of what a player carries.

On the ice, his first year in Washington started fast. He has 11 goals in 18 games, playing 19 minutes a night against strong competition (Evolving-Hockey had him in the 95th percentile last season). The Capitals take 56.7% of the expected goals with him at five on five, a real number, and he is 15th in the league in wins added by his goals.

Now the cooling. Eleven goals on 8.4 expected means he is shooting 24%, against 17% last season, and that rate rarely lasts. He has no goals in his last four games, and only two assists all season, which is odd for a player All Three Zones tracking pegged as a setup man (8.7 primary shot assists per 60 last season). If the goals slow, the passing should start showing up on the scoresheet. Back in Buffalo, people are still saying the Sabres never replaced him.
headline: Tuch's new team, new son, same shot
